content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - GPU serving pool 'gpu-a' saturation. queue_depth=9800, token_throttle=true, p50_latency=1.2s, p99_latency=9.8s. triggered autoscaler alert. paging oncall.

carmen: ack'ing. i'm oncall but in transit, will check from phone. what's the customer impact? any external pages?

dave: seeing sustained queue growth since ~10m ago on the inference router. many requests are throttled (429) to downstream. affected customers: a handful of high-throughput tenants on dedicated capacity + some hosted API traffic routed to gpu-a via smart routing.

carmen: ok. can you paste the autoscaler logs and any node errors? i'm triaging.

dave: autoscaler: `scaleUp failed: hit maxNodeCount for pool gpu-a (max=18, requested=22)`

dave: also seeing repeated node flaps in the last 8m, drivers restarting on three nodes. snippet from node logs:
```
[driver] nvidia: GPU 0: device memory exhausted
[driver] nvidia: Xid 79: Process info unavailable
kernel: nvidia_uvm: UVM fault: OOM while allocating 0x100000
```

gen-runtime-ryan: quick note: Xid 79 in our infra has historically correlated with driver OOMs and heavy memcpy storms when batches spike. kernel module may be killing contexts, reducing effective GPU capacity.

carmen: so autoscaler wants to scale but maxNodes prevents it, and existing nodes are flapping -> effective capacity lower than expected. checklist: is there any recent deploy to runtime/driver config?

eng-runtime-ryan: no driver rollout in last 24h. changed scheduling bump yesterday for continuous batching but that was small. i'm pulling dmesg + kube events.

sre-lead-jen: oncall, please consider immediate mitigations: 1) divert new traffic off gpu-a, 2) cordon/flaky nodes, 3) fallback to CPU/light models for noisy tenants, 4) escalate capacity limit with infra if possible.

carmen: starting manual routing change: updating smart-routing policy to deprioritize gpu-a for non-SLA tenants. will keep dedicated customer routes unless they request fallback.

support-lucia: notifying impacted customers on status page: "Investigating GPU capacity issues causing elevated latencies/429s. Temporary mitigations in progress." posting now.

dave: cordoning nodes with driver restarts: node-17, node-21, node-12. running:
```
kubectl cordon node-17
kubectl drain node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
systemctl restart nvidia-driver
```

dave: drain helped on node-17 but node-21 failed to come back: `nvidia-driver.service: start operation timed out` and then kernel reported Xid 79 during probe.

eng-runtime-ryan: trying a graceful driver reload sequence on node-21, if that fails we may need to evict and reprovision. also checking whether a single tenant is causing large allocations: sampling pod memory/GPU usage.

carmen: watching queue: reduced ingress after routing change, but p99 still high. autoscaler still at maxNodes so cannot add capacity automatically.

sre-lead-jen: do we have emergency capacity (burst pool) that bypasses maxNodes? Ops has a soft quota on some pools, we might be able to request immediate burst, but it needs manual approval.

oncall-marc: i'm joining. marc here, taking handoff from carmen. summary: gpu-a saturated, autoscaler blocked by pool limit, multiple nodes flapping due to driver OOM/Xid 79. current mitigations: traffic deprioritized, three nodes cordoned/draining, support notified customers. plan to attempt temporary burst and further node reprovision if needed.

oncall-marc: @infra-team can you approve a one-time increase to pool gpu-a to 24 nodes? we need to lift maxNodeCount to let autoscaler catch up and absorb backlog.

sre-lead-jen: pinging infra/allocs. also we should consider a model-level fallback: route heavy requests to a quantized L2 model to reduce per-token memory.

eng-runtime-ryan: patch ready to route noisy tenants to quantized variant (low_mem=true). can deploy a canary in 2m. recommending also enabling prefix KV caching eviction to free mem.

dave: canary deployed for 3 tenants. initial results: GPU mem pressure dropped ~35% on those pods.

oncall-marc: infra approved temporary +6 nodes (manual approval). updating pool maxNodes and triggering scale-up.

incident-bot: autoscaler event: scaleUp request accepted, launching 6 nodes for pool gpu-a. expected join ~5m.

dave: note: even with additional nodes, if driver module on node image is corrupted we might get flaps on new nodes. provisioning with stable driver image tag: `driver:v3.4.1-stable`.

eng-runtime-ryan: rolling image to driver:v3.4.1-stable for new nodes and restarting failed nodes with same tag.

support-lucia: updating customers: "We have initiated automatic scaling and temporary model fallbacks; some traffic still experiencing high latencies. Next update in 20 minutes."

dave: new nodes joining, but one new node shows `nvidia_uvm UVM fault` during initialization and gets marked NotReady. marking it cordoned to avoid routing.

oncall-marc: good catch. keep cordoning flaky nodes. if more than 10% of pool fails on init, we need to stop provisioning and investigate image/driver bundle.

eng-runtime-ryan: collecting full kernel logs and raising a debug build to reproduce locally. initial theory: continuous batching + large request shapes hitting a kernel-path in driver leading to UVM allocation blowups. open ticket: RUNTIME-1459.

sre-lead-jen: action items: 1) eng-runtime reproduce & fix (RUNTIME-1459), 2) infra review node image & driver packaging, 3) product evaluate routing policy defaults (prevent all heavy hosted traffic to single pool), 4) ops define burst approval runbook. assign owners.

oncall-marc: i'm taking incident lead. carmen handing off full-context. carmen: anything else before you go?

carmen: all good. i put logs and short dump in the #incidents-logs bucket and linked them in the thread. thank you team, back to regular duties.

support-lucia: scheduled a customer conference for top impacted tenant for 3pm to explain mitigations and timeline.

dave: current status (summary): queue depth down from 9800 -> 1200, p50 ~380ms, p99 ~2.3s. several nodes cordoned, +6 nodes requested and partially joined, autoscaler resumed. flappable nodes still under investigation.

oncall-marc: leaving this thread open for next update. i'll post a status update in 15m. if anyone sees regression or additional Xid patterns, ping me directly. cc: @sre-lead-jen @eng-runtime-ryan

sre-lead-jen: adding postmortem lead: eng-runtime-ryan. timeline and RCA to follow. temporary mitigations documented in incident runbook.

incident-bot: incident state: active -> mitigated. severity downgraded to SEV3. close criteria: stable p99 < 1s and no node flaps for 30m.

oncall-marc: noted. next check-in 15m. thanks everyone for the quick responses.
